evidence.note: The Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy places this work in its working chronology of Plato's authentic dialogues; it separates spuria/dubia and notes that most dialogues in the accepted group are now only rarely doubted.

Schofield's Routledge Encyclopedia treatment isolates the live authenticity problems (including Alcibiades I, Hippias Major, Clitophon/Theages and Letter VII) rather than this work; it notes that most major dialogues have strong ancient attestation.

rationale: Apology of Socrates belongs to the core set of dialogues treated as genuinely Platonic in current reference scholarship and is not a live authorship problem comparable to the project's B/C/D cases. A records strong scholarly acceptance, not certainty about chronology or the identification of any character's speech with Plato's own beliefs.
